clue.text: Vine is withering around start of winter month on the fence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap about the month and its first day
something withering shrivels and loses its shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: December is abbreviated DEC
the start of a month is its 1st, with I as the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a vine shrivelling at the beginning of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withering' turns VINE IS into INSIVE, which goes 'around' DECI, December the 1st.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting on the fence cannot make up their mind, which is being irresolute.

clue.text: Ostensibly good claim made by warrior band

definitions.meaning: read as ..., someone claiming to be pious, which may be only a show

explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu military regiment or armed troop is known by this term.

clue.text: After reflection, bar entry to multiple crash site

indicators.note: reflected in a mirror, so the bar is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a bar

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, the police bar entry to a pile-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' here means sleep; a dormitory is where you crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang crash means to sleep, so a dormitory is a place to do it.

clue.text: Tory banker on piano with pretentious band of entertainers

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative
a banker is a racing certainty, a cert
P is the musical marking for soft, piano
arty means affectedly artistic

explanation.surface: A Conservative financier plays the piano alongside a pretentious ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is a sure bet in British betting slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe of performers giving variety shows, popular in wartime Britain.

clue.text: A little pasta and pepper?

definitions.meaning: conchiglie are small pasta pieces shaped like seashells
to pepper is to bombard with shot, as artillery does

explanation.definitionFit: A pasta shape, and a verb for bombarding a target with gunfire.

clue.text: Giant artillery division invading very historic Russian city

indicators.note: the giant and gunners go inside the word for historic

parts.note: something historic is old
Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A huge artillery force invades an ancient Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historic' is OLD here, and 'invading' sets the giant and the gunners between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Volga formerly named Stalingrad, scene of the great siege.

clue.text: What's attached to hook or needle

definitions.meaning: an angler fixes a worm or lure on the hook to tempt a fish
to needle someone is to tease or provoke them

explanation.definitionFit: Lure on an angler's hook, and also a verb for goading or taunting someone.

clue.text: Process one introduced to heavy metal plant bearing fruit? Not at first

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold, a heavy metal

indicators.note: the numeral is put inside the plant's word

parts.note: the tomato plant bears fruit
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A factory process brings a heavy-metal plant into fruit-bearing, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' looks like rock music but is gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Using machines to carry out a procedure without human labour.

clue.text: Lord with doctor shortly touring developing nations

indicators.note: travelling about, so the letters go round into a new order

parts.note: DR is the short form of doctor

explanation.surface: A peer and his physician go on a tour of poorer countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges LORD, WITH and DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorer, less industrialised countries were once grouped under this name.

clue.text: Writer's work revolving around fugitive's confession — hollow

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the writer

indicators.note: the turned work goes about the outside of the confession and the hollow
turning round, so the abbreviation for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
someone on the run would admit 'I ran'
a dell is a small wooded hollow

explanation.surface: A novelist's book turns on a runaway's admission, which rings empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns the work round and 'around' wraps it about the confession and the hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was an Italian dramatist and novelist, a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Regularly tip up the flipping box

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the picked letters are read backwards
taking every other letter of the phrase, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone irritably tells another to tip up the wretched box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of TIP UP THE, giving IUTE, and 'flipping' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental case for needles and similar items, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Published feature: "Journey on Wagon" penned by "Anon"

indicators.note: enclosed as if in a pen by the word that follows

parts.note: anon is an old word meaning soon
a trip is a journey
a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an anonymous article titled 'Journey on Wagon'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anon' looks like an anonymous author but is the old word for soon; 'penned by' wraps it round the journey and wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip printed in a paper is a published feature.

clue.text: With flares and alarm both, Henry put out to sea

parts.note: a bell is a warning signal

indicators.note: the letter for the unit is dismissed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written
MED is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, both alarmed and ablaze with signal flares, is cast adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flares' looks like distress signals, but they are wide-legged trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers flared below the knee, as sailors wore, are described this way.

clue.text: Game runners, entering at risk, providing some hope

indicators.note: the governing body goes inside the little word

parts.note: the FA, Football Association, runs the game in England
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Football's governing body taking a gamble may offer a little hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases are used ironically: 'some hope' and 'a fat chance' both mean no hope at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic expressions for very little likelihood of success.

clue.text: Fifties doctor filling peach with hydrogen gas only

indicators.note: the fifties and doctor go inside the peach

parts.note: a peach or beaut is something excellent
L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two of them
MO is a medical officer
H is the symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A 1950s doctor fills a peach with hydrogen gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' here is idle talk, not a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is all talk and no action is said to be this.

clue.text: Bases old show around right sort of programming

indicators.note: the right letter has the bases placed about it

parts.note: feet are the bases a body stands on
to air something is to show it publicly

explanation.surface: A TV schedule built on an old show revolves around one kind of programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R inside FEET to make FREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts that anyone can receive without a subscription are described by this term.

clue.text: Making elaborate attempt finally in support of suspect on remand

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other
suspect means dubious, so the letters are put into doubt and rearranged
only the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An elaborate attempt is made to support a suspect held on remand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges ON REMAND to ADORNMEN, with T below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating or embellishing something is ornamentation.

clue.text: Opening fortnightly set back stores

indicators.note: set back means the held letters are read from the far end
the word holds the letters within it, as a store keeps goods

explanation.surface: A shop's grand opening is postponed by a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' finds ORTNI inside the word, and 'set back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory passage at the start of a song or talk is an opening.

clue.text: City girl who's poorly turned out to have retracted blood type

indicators.note: drawn back, so the slovenly woman's word is read backwards

parts.note: an old sense of slut is a slovenly, untidy woman
A is one of the ABO blood groups

explanation.surface: A city girl looking unwell withdraws from giving blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly turned out' means badly dressed, not ill; 'retracted' reads the girl backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: Conservative group getting on train

parts.note: getting on in years means aged
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Tory party members board a train together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like the political party, but here it means traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionalists who keep to established ways are collectively called this.

clue.text: Lower-division player training and maybe playing rallies Palace

parts.note: a ham is a poor actor, a player of the lowest rank
PT is physical training
tennis rallies are played on court

explanation.surface: A lower-league footballer trains and plays at Crystal Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace' suggests the football club; HAMPTON COURT is Henry VIII's palace by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tudor royal residence in south-west London, famous for its maze.

clue.text: A plug, say, having this might not be so beneficial

definitions.text: A plug, say, having this might not be so beneficial

parts.words: A plug, say, having this might not be so beneficial
parts.note: split the phrase as nought plus the protective wire in a plug: a plug with zero protection would be no help

explanation.definitionFit: Something useful or helpful is beneficial, of benefit to its user.

clue.text: Average travel expense declared by the Speaker

indicators.note: spoken out loud by someone, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a fare is the cost of a journey

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker announces typical travel claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Speaker' suggests the Commons, but just means someone talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, neither good nor bad, as in a fair performance.

clue.text: Head has left Foundation unchanged

indicators.note: the leading letter has departed from the word

parts.note: a basis is a foundation

explanation.surface: The head of a school has quit and the foundation stays the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold without alteration or guarantee, in its present state.

clue.text: Chaste woman hugging not a thing that is itself common

definitions.note: a word that is itself a common one, as a common noun

indicators.note: the chaste woman wraps her arms round the zero

parts.note: a nun takes a vow of chastity
nothing, shown as the round letter like zero

explanation.surface: A celibate woman embraces nothing worldly, an ordinary thing herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' is the grammarian's sense: a common noun names a kind of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes words naming things as common or proper nouns.

clue.text: Job one arranged with EU — alas the French bottle it

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A job in Brussels is lamented, and the French keep their wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges JOB, I, EU and ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaujolais is a French red wine from Burgundy, bottled there.

clue.text: One standing for election's first on radio repeat

definitions.text: One standing for election's first on radio
definitions.meaning: in the radio alphabet the first letter of election, E, is spoken as this code word

explanation.definitionFit: The NATO alphabet's word for E, and also a reverberating sound coming back.

clue.text: Dogs not giving way hit by front of bus when crossing road

indicators.note: the stern word is struck into by the bus's front letter

parts.note: stern means firm and unyielding

indicators.note: the first letter of the vehicle
the road goes across, inside the conjunction

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Stubborn dogs that won't give way are struck by a bus crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit by' drives the bus's front letter into the stern word; 'crossing' runs the road through 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Large Alpine mountain-rescue dogs are of this breed.
